property.name: dfs.replication
property.description: Every block is stored on all 3 DataNodes (one copy per laptop).

property.name: dfs.blocksize
property.description: 128 MB blocks: 2019-Nov.csv (~9.0 GB) is about 68 blocks and 2019-Oct.csv (~5.7 GB) about 43 blocks, so Spark gets ~111 input splits.

property.name: dfs.namenode.name.dir
property.description: NameNode metadata (fsimage + edits). Used on master only.

property.name: dfs.namenode.rpc-bind-host
property.description: Listen on all interfaces, so DataNodes can connect even if "master" resolves to a loopback address on master itself.

property.name: dfs.namenode.secondary.http-address
property.description: Explicit host (the default 0.0.0.0 makes start-dfs.sh try "ssh 0.0.0.0").

property.name: dfs.namenode.datanode.registration.ip-hostname-check
property.description: Laptops have no reverse DNS; /etc/hosts is enough.

property.name: dfs.client.block.write.replace-datanode-on-failure.policy
property.description: Recommended by Hadoop for clusters of 3 nodes or fewer: with replication=3 and 3 DataNodes there is no spare node to swap in, so the default policy would abort writes when one laptop drops off Wi-Fi. The NameNode re-replicates the missing copy when the node returns.

property.name: dfs.datanode.du.reserved
property.description: Keep 10 GB per laptop free for the OS and Spark shuffle spill.

property.name: dfs.permissions.enabled
property.description: The three laptops may use different Linux user names. Turning HDFS permission checks off avoids AccessControlException when Spark executors (running as each laptop's user) write Iceberg files. Lab cluster only.

property.name: dfs.webhdfs.enabled
property.description: Lets the NameNode UI file browser list and download files.
